editorial.headline: Transport and Machinery Design: Nationally Open, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Industrial design for vehicles, machinery and their components is open to foreign investment nationally, but Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium means it cannot be registered there today.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor, the defining fact is geographic: this activity can be foreign-owned nationally, but it cannot be registered for PMA in Bali today. Bali blocks it under its island-wide, permanent moratorium on Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA. In this case, OSS places every scope of the activity in those risk bands at the Besar, or large-business, scale. The Bali restriction is therefore direct, even though the national position is open.

The activity is industrial design for products, production-support equipment and components used in transport equipment and machinery. Its brief is unusually broad: designs may concern bicycles and animal-drawn vehicles; handcarts, pushcarts, prams, wheelchairs and stretchers; rail vehicles; chairlifts and ski lifts; elevators and lifting equipment; and motor vehicles, ships, aircraft and spacecraft. It also includes the design of tyres, anti-slip chains, vehicle components and accessories, as well as machines, pumps, compressors, agricultural and construction machinery, and textile machinery. The design work may also be carried out using specialised software.

This is a registration space for industrial-design businesses working across those product categories, and it is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. Nationally, the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, so the record does not impose a foreign-equity reduction for this activity. That national openness is the relevant answer for an investor considering the activity in Indonesia as a whole; it is not, however, an answer that transfers automatically to Bali.

Bali’s position is more definite. The provincial moratorium cited in the record, dated May 13, 2026, blocks PMA registration where the applicable risk class is Low or Medium-Low, and it applies island-wide on a permanent basis. For this activity, that condition is met across every scope at the large scale. The practical reading is clear: national policy permits full foreign ownership, while Bali does not permit a foreign-owned registration for the activity today.
